title: Cahier de Topos
subtitle: The site, the topos, the category — the instrument Grothendieck built before he knew what he would do with it
rationale: The Montpellier inventory has no group called “Topos”: the leaves carrying the word are scattered. Two folders are titled with nothing else (19 and 161-3); a duality of topoi sits among the notes around Pursuing Stacks (115); a stratified topos is dated 1981 (151); and the categorical layer that makes any of it legible lies elsewhere again (161-1, 161-2, 135). This book is therefore a grouping of our own, and is flagged as such. The thread it follows is a notion that changed sense three times under its author's hand — a generalised neighbourhood in SGA 4, then a geometric object in its own right, then, late, a kind of space.

sections.title: The two folders titled “Topos”
sections.intro: The only folders Grothendieck labelled with that word alone. Nothing in them gives a date: the range the archivists propose is deduced from the versos.

sections.title: The categorical footing
sections.intro: A topos does not read without the categories carrying it. These three folders are the corresponding working notes, including one the inventory could not decide between “universal algebra” and “categories”.

sections.title: Around SGA 4
sections.intro: The fundamental group, and the leftover drafting of SGA 4. This is where the notion was born, inside a text meant for publication — and these leaves are its draft.

sections.title: The late topoi
sections.intro: Twenty years on the notion returns, in functorial duality and then stratified. In the inventory these leaves also belong to “Around Pursuing Stacks” and to “Stratified spaces”.

title: Cahier de Motifs
subtitle: The theory he never published, and of which almost everything that survives is here
rationale: This book reproduces one inventory group exactly — “Théorie des motifs”, folders 10 to 18 — adding nothing and removing nothing. It is the simplest and most valuable case: the grouping is Grothendieck's, not ours. Motives gave rise to no publication of his; these 946 manuscript leaves are, for the most part, the theory itself.

sections.title: Théorie des motifs
sections.intro: The group as the inventory gives it, in filing order: from tensor categories to the relation with Hodge theory, by way of the motivic Galois group and the standard conjectures.

title: La Longue Marche
subtitle: Fifteen hundred pages written in one stretch through Galois theory, and what accreted around them
rationale: Two inventory groups, taken as they stand: the work itself (folder 140, cut in four by the archivists to fit ten-centimetre boxes) and “Autour de La Longue Marche” (141 to 149). The split into 140-1 through 140-4 is thus a packing constraint, not a division by the author: the pagination running continuously from 1 to 787 says as much.

sections.title: The work
sections.intro: A draft, then pages 1 to 292, then the second part — “variations on the equation of loops” — and the rest through to page 787. The pagination is Grothendieck's; the brackets are the archivists'.

sections.title: Around the Long March
sections.intro: Teichmüller above all, and what Grothendieck called his “Teichmülleries”: the Galois action on Teichmüller groupoids, the paradigms of algebraic curves, the structure at infinity of the Mg,ν.

title: Cahiers tardifs
subtitle: 1986–1991: the last great drafts, written day by day and dated day by day — the Dérivateurs excepted, which already have an edition.
rationale: The inventory keeps “Vers une géométrie des formes” (156) and “Dérivateurs” (157) apart; putting them under one tab is our doing. What holds them together is not the subject but the manner: these are the only folders in the fonds where nearly every chapter carries its date, sometimes to the day — 5 June, 6 June, 8 June 1986 — because Grothendieck was then writing as one keeps a journal. It is also the last state of his hand before the withdrawal of 1991, and the material most favourable to anyone who wants to read the mathematics together with the reflection that accompanies it. The Dérivateurs are named here and not listed: Künzer, Malgoire and Maltsiniotis have transcribed all 2,135 leaves of them, and there is no version of this project that improves on that. What this tab offers is the material nobody has edited.

sections.title: Vers une géométrie des formes (1986)
sections.intro: Nine chapters written between 5 June and 15 July 1986, four of them successive “moutures” of one Analysis situs. To see the four in sequence is to watch a thought correct itself.

sections.title: Dérivateurs (1990–1991)
sections.intro: Nineteen chapters, 2,135 leaves: the last great mathematical draft, left in manuscript and unfinished.

sections.title: Around the Dérivateurs
sections.intro: The last dated folder in the fonds, which the archivists place around 1990–1991.

title: Notes techniques dispersées
subtitle: The thirty-five folders that belong to no work — a question taken up, settled or abandoned, and filed alone
rationale: The inventory files these at the top level, inside no thematic group of its own: they are what is left when every named run — Cristaux, Motifs, SGA, Picard, the Long March — has been accounted for. Gathering them is our doing, and the only thing they have in common is that nothing else claimed them. That is precisely their interest. A folder that joined no work is usually a question Grothendieck took up on its own, pushed as far as it would go in twenty or two hundred leaves, and then left: analytic spaces in 1961, local cohomology in 1967, systems of pseudo-lines in 1984. Two top-level folders are left out, being no kind of technical note — folder 139, which is the Émile Picard medal itself, and folder 162-1, a list of papers lent out.

sections.title: Before the schemes (1953–1962)
sections.intro: The earliest leaves in the fonds, and the only ones from the years of the thesis. Folder 1 is functional analysis — the subject he made his name in and then left.

sections.title: Around the schemes (1960–1971)
sections.intro: The IHÉS years, minus everything that went into EGA, SGA or a named run. What remains is the working residue: a construction attempted, a duality checked, a seminar written up.

sections.title: After the departure (1972–1984)
sections.intro: Isolated notes from the Montpellier years, when the long works were Pursuing Stacks and the Long March and these were what he did beside them. The combinatorial turn shows here — maps, word types, pseudo-lines.

sections.title: Undated
sections.intro: No date on the leaves and no verso to infer one from. Three folders the archivists could place nowhere in time.
